newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas quiet ahead of Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas quiet ahead of Taiwan.

text.p: Gasoline traders were sidelined on Tuesday ahead of the close of Taiwan's buy tender.
"We are more interested in the CPC tender," said a seller which had been offering on the fixed price fob Singapore market on Monday.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp's (CPC) tender to buy 250,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate for delivery between September 1-15 to Keelung, Kaohsiung, Shalung or Taichung, closes July 29 and is valid for two days.
But some Singapore refiners said they were not interested in the tender as they had no barrels or that previous winners into the tender were too aggressive.
In its last reformate tender, CPC bought one cargo at $23.30 per barrel, c-and-f Taiwan for delivery August 11-20 from a Dutch trader, traders said.
The same trader had earlier sold to CPC two August 1-10 delivery cargoes at $24.60 and $24.76.
Offers into the current tender should be slightly below $25, or around $1.00 higher than Singapore 95-octane fob quotes.
Unleaded 95-octane was traded on Monday at $23.80.
Singapore naphtha was talked sideways despite the overnight fall in crude and weak demand, but on the back of supported Japanese open-spec levels at $209/$210 per tonne for second-half September.
August naphtha swaps were last quoted at five cents per barrel firmer at $21.90/$21.95 from Monday.
Traders in Japan said prices held steady due to active support in the north Asian market and firmer European prices.
But fundamentally, traders said demand from endusers was lacklustre.
"Korean and Japanese petchems are facing tanktops," a South Korean refiner said. "It is hard to find requirements for August and September."
